comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C33-C40 regarding BtaR1 mutant fitness advantage in broth. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED, with OpenEval highlighting statistical significance and convergent evidence, while peer reviewers found it 'straightforward and interesting' without concerns.

Complete agreement on claims C41-C43 regarding agar plate competition results. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers requested figure improvements but accepted the underlying data showing contact-dependent constraint.

Disagreement on claims C28, C51-C56 regarding T6SS toxin/immunity gene regulation. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED based on transcriptomics and established knowledge, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting ectopic expression experiments to identify specific toxin/immunity pairs and criticizing Figure 2A presentation.

Disagreement on claims C57-C60 regarding T6SS-1-mediated killing mechanism. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN and request additional control experiments (T6SS mutant as inhibitor versus tle1 mutant) to demonstrate the mechanism more conclusively.

Both address genetic evidence for T6SS-1 role (C61-C64), with both finding evidence SUPPORTED. However, peer review R5 also includes broader policing claims (C3, C5, C65-C66) that OpenEval addresses separately in R6. Both accept the complementation experiments without major concerns.

Partial overlap on central policing mechanism claims. OpenEval R6 covers C2-C3, C5-C6, C30, C65-C67, while peer R6 covers C6-C7, C30, C67, C78-C79. Both find evidence SUPPORTED and recognize this as the main finding, though peer reviewers note need for clarification on specific toxin/immunity genes.
OpenEval R6 includes claims C3, C5, C65-C66 that peer R5 also addresses. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED, showing agreement on the genetic evidence supporting the policing mechanism through T6SS-1.

Partial overlap on novelty and significance claims (C7, C78-C79). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED for broader significance, and peer reviewers also accept this as 'straightforward and interesting' main finding (SUPPORTED).

Partial overlap on metabolic cost interpretation (C4, C76). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes C4 includes untested speculation, while peer reviewers accepted the metabolic cost interpretation without requesting additional evidence.
Both address claim C77 regarding inference about BtaR2/BtaR3 mutants. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers accepting this inference based on lack of fitness effects in competitions.

Minimal overlap on claim C68 regarding mechanistic interpretation. OpenEval finds broader significance claims SUPPORTED, while peer R7 focuses on metabolic cost (C4, C68, C76) and finds evidence SUPPORTED.
OpenEval evaluated claims C45-C46 regarding CDI not being responsible for policing effect (SUPPORTED). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.
